text:
Victor Eklund is the Islanders rookie who keeps showing up around the net. The 16th pick of the 2025 draft has five goals and eight points in 16 games, and twice already he has scored in back-to-back games. Stefen Rosner of NHL.com described his goal against the Devils as Eklund, "the dog that he is," getting his stick on a loose puck. That's a fair scouting report.

He's ahead of the curve. Forwards picked 11th to 21st since 2005 averaged 0.32 points a game in their first full season; Eklund is at 0.50. The Islanders take about 53% of the expected goals with him on the ice, which is better than the team overall, and he has been playing beside Brayden Schenn.

The part to temper is shooting. He's at 20.8% on 24 shots, well above the 14% we'd expect him to settle near, and five goals on 3.9 expected. Our range is wide, 14 to 27 goals over a full season, as it should be for a 20-year-old. The habits look real. The shooting percentage won't last.
headline: Eklund finds the loose pucks
